title: A shape's border arrives the same colour as its fill, so turning it up shows nothing
goal: Draw a box and drag its Border width up and nothing appears to happen: the box just gets bigger. The border is there, it is simply painted the exact colour the fill already is, so there is no line to see until you also go and change its colour. A first border should read as a border.
notes:
Found on 2026-09-08 while repairing the five stale border walks. Reproduced on the probe build at 0ef9bd9f.

Command (walk body saved at /tmp/pz-probe/border-invisible.json: blank 900x600, key r, drag 340,300 to 560,460, press Slider in Border across 0.3, panelMenu Border choose Outside, render, press Color in Border, panel):

  Scripts/playtest.sh /tmp/pz-probe/border-invisible.json --no-build

Output:
  border picker swatch marked as current: [{'detail': '#FF2114, already picked', 'name': 'Shades 5'}]
  fill centre pixel: (255, 59, 48)
  11pt outside border pixel: (255, 59, 48)

The panel at that moment reads Fill (red swatch), Border > Color (the same red swatch), Position Outside, Width 11 pt. An 11 pt outside ring painted in the fill colour is invisible on white, and the only visible effect of dragging Width is that the shape grows.

This is why corner-radius-rounds-walk and ellipse-border-walk now have to press the Border Color well and pick Shades 9 before their ring is legible: without it the walk passes while photographing nothing. Those two walks are the regression test to keep honest if this changes.

A shape arrives at Width 0, so nobody sees the clash until they pull the slider. Likely fix is in the arriving style (PhotonzCore AnnotationStyles.arrivingStyle(forShape:)) or wherever a new layer's border colour is seeded: a first border wants a colour that contrasts with the fill rather than a copy of it. Whether that should be a fixed ink, a darker shade of the fill, or the last border colour you used is a UX judgment, hence p2 and not a silent fix.
acceptance: Drawing a shape and dragging its Border width off zero puts a line on screen you can see against the fill, with no second trip to the colour well
The border colour a shape arrives with is still whatever you last left a border on that kind of shape, so the memory rule is not undone
A walk proves it: the pixel under an outside border is a different colour from the pixel inside the fill

log.note: Reproduced on the probe at f0dd48b1. Walk /tmp/pz-probe/arrive.json (blank 900x600, key r, drag 340,300 to 560,460, render, panel): the panel reads Fill on, Effects > Border on, Inside, Width 4 pt, and the render's box is one flat colour. Scanning the render at y=380 (through the middle of the box, NOT y=300 which sits on its top edge) gives `0:#FFFFFF 340:#FF543E 560:#FFFFFF` — no rim. With the border painted a deeper shade the same scan gives `340:#BD1D00 344:#FF543E 556:#BD1D00 560:#FFFFFF`, so the ring is 4 px and only its colour was hiding it.

Cause is the arriving defaults, not the plumbing: ShapeDefaults.standard(for:) seeds a box/oval with fill = colorHex = #FF3B30, and AnnotationStyles.arrivingStyle(forShape:) hands the Border effect that same stroke paint. Nothing is copying the fill onto the border at draw time; the two simply start equal.

Adversarial review of the idea, before building: the equal colours are deliberate, not a slip — switch Fill off and the shape is an outline box in the shape colour, which is where the shared 'shape colour' comes from. And the decision resolved earlier today (outline-leaves-appearance-...) chose option a on the promise that 'nothing you draw changes'. Making every fresh box arrive with a visible rim changes what every fresh box looks like, which is a visual direction call and contradicts a four-hour-old answer. So this is not a silent fix; it is a decision.

Decision filed with four options and real app pictures for three of them (deeper shade of the fill / near-black ink / no edge until asked / leave it), rendered from the probe by picking the Border colour through the panel rather than mocked up. Recommended: a deeper shade of the fill.

For whoever builds the answer: the change belongs in ShapeDefaults.standard(for:) (and, for option a, a small darken-or-lighten helper in PhotonzCore with tests). The memory rule needs no change — AnnotationStyles.remember() already lifts a border's colour onto the tool, so the second shape onward keeps whatever you last left. Acceptance item 3 wants a walk; write it as Scripts/playtest/border-reads-as-a-border-walk.json with a render and a scan at the box's mid height, and keep corner-radius-rounds-walk and ellipse-border-walk honest (they currently press the Border Color well to get a legible ring, which the fix may make unnecessary).

Reproduced (fresh box: Border on, Inside, 4 pt, painted the fill colour, no rim in the render). The fix is a visual direction call - it changes what every newly drawn shape looks like, and it cuts against today's answer that nothing you draw changes - so a decision is open with four options and real app pictures. Recommended: a deeper shade of the fill.
